facts.title: Mooncake: A KVCache-centric Disaggregated Architecture for LLM Serving
facts.event_hint: Production serving platform (Kimi/Moonshot AI) disclosing a KVCache-centric disaggregated LLM serving architecture with prefill/decode separation and a disaggregated KV cache distributed across the CPU/DRAM/SSD of the GPU cluster.
facts.problem: LLM serving under long-context, high-load conditions is bottlenecked by KVCache reuse and SLO attainment; monolithic GPU serving leaves CPU/DRAM/SSD resources underutilized and cannot separately scale prefill vs. decode, causing throughput collapse under overload.
facts.mechanism: KVCache-centric disaggregation: (1) separates prefill and decode clusters; (2) leverages underutilized CPU/DRAM/SSD on the GPU cluster to form a disaggregated KVCache store; (3) a KVCache-centric scheduler balances effective throughput against TTFT/TBT SLOs; (4) a prediction-based early rejection policy handles overload instead of admitting and violating SLOs.

evidence.claim: Up to a 525% increase in throughput in certain simulated scenarios while adhering to SLOs.
Mooncake enables Kimi to handle 75% more requests under real workloads.
Architecture leverages underutilized CPU, DRAM, and SSD of the GPU cluster to implement a disaggregated KVCache.

facts.evaluation_context: Production deployment at Moonshot AI serving Kimi; complemented by simulated throughput experiments. No model size, hardware spec, or absolute latency numbers in abstract.
facts.limitations: Evidence is abstract-level; full paper body not fetched, so simulated-scenario conditions and baseline method details are unverified. Real-world 75% figure lacks absolute request-rate or hardware context.
facts.project_relevance: Directly the canonical reference for TPN-style inference-network / PD-disaggregation. The disaggregated KVCache across CPU/DRAM/SSD and the cross-node KV transfer it implies are the central workload for which KVCache cross-node transfer, DPU/SmartNIC offload, and CXL/disaggregated-memory paths are being designed. A must-track anchor paper for the briefing's TPN and Agent-acceleration (code-graph / parallel-speculative) tracks since modern agent serving inherits Kimi-style long-context overload.
